label: Premium electric car
motion: India will leapfrog to electric cars faster than most forecasts suggest.
ground_reality: Society committees often block charger installation; renters have no vote.
Resale is priced on battery health, and buyers still ask 'kitna chalega?'
Dealers bundle insurance, accessories and 'handling' into the on-road price.
Test drives are concentrated in metros; tier-3 buyers buy from photos and YouTube.
malpractices: Booking amount parked for months with no delivery date.
Charging installer claims subsidy and disappears.
pro_claims: Running cost is already 4-6x cheaper per km; the total cost of ownership crosses petrol at ~8,000 km/year.
Charging infrastructure is following early adopters, not preceding them.
Tier-2 buyers are the fastest-growing EV car segment in 2026.
con_claims: A ₹22 lakh car is a status purchase; the buyer is not optimising for fuel savings.
Resale and battery risk are unpriced, and the second owner bears it.
Apartment charging is the real bottleneck, not range.

label: Electric two-wheeler
motion: The electric scooter is the real Indian EV transition, not the car.
ground_reality: The real buyer is a 28-year-old rider doing 40-60 km/day, not a tech enthusiast.
Battery replacement at year 4-5 is the moment trust is won or lost.
Local service is everything; a two-week wait kills a brand in a district.
Financing at 18-24% is common for buyers outside prime credit.
malpractices: Dealers suppress battery health and range in used sales.
Unauthorised 'subsidy agents' charge fees for free applications.
Service centres replace whole modules instead of repair.
Fake range claims in YouTube ads.
pro_claims: At 40 km/day, an e-scooter saves ₹30,000-40,000 a year in fuel and maintenance.
The buyer already trusts the local dealer; the category is crossing the chasm in tier-2/3.
Financing innovation, not subsidy, is the real unlock.
con_claims: Battery replacement wipes out the savings if the buyer keeps the vehicle beyond 4 years.
Service deserts outside the top 100 cities still break the promise.
The cheapest e-scooters are a quality lottery.

label: 10-minute quick commerce
motion: Quick commerce will hollow out the neighbourhood kirana within five years.
ground_reality: 10-minute delivery works because the worker absorbs the risk, not because the model is magic.
Kirana credit is a financial service; quick commerce is a convenience service. They are not substitutes for everyone.
Dark stores are concentrated in dense, high-income pin codes; tier-3 is mostly a delivery-radius story on paper.
Expiry, pest and cold-chain violations surface when audits tighten.
malpractices: Surge and handling fees revealed at checkout.
Dark patterns: pre-selected add-ons, false urgency, subscription traps.
Gig workers penalised for traffic and building delays.
pro_claims: Convenience is not a discount; it is a new category of demand, especially for urban dual-income households.
The kirana's credit and relationship moat is real, but it does not cover late-night or 500-item baskets.
Dark-store density, not delivery speed, is the actual unit-economics lever.
con_claims: The 10-minute promise externalises safety and labour costs onto riders.
Kirana is not dying; it is being squeezed in the top 8-10% of baskets.
Once discounts stop, habit may not survive a 20% price gap.

label: UPI in small-town India
price_note: Free for users; merchant discount rate varies
motion: UPI has solved rural payment inclusion; trust is now the only barrier.
ground_reality: The QR code is trusted; the phone call asking for a PIN is not.
Feature-phone users and shared devices remain outside the funnel.
Dispute resolution is the real adoption barrier, not literacy.
Digital arrest and 'electricity bill' scams are now mainstream.
malpractices: Screen-sharing scams under the guise of KYC.
pro_claims: UPI is now 85% of India's digital payment volume; the network effect is irreversible.
Rural users adopt through merchants and family, not app store rankings.
Fraud is a trust tax, not a reason to retreat to cash.
con_claims: The last 15% is the hardest: feature phones, shared devices, low literacy and no dispute recourse.
A single high-profile fraud can freeze a village's adoption for months.
Free UPI for users does not mean free for merchants or the ecosystem.

label: AI and white-collar jobs
motion: AI will destroy more Indian white-collar jobs than it creates by 2030.
ground_reality: The threat is task-level, not job-level, but the anxiety is job-level.
Tier-2 graduates face an English + tooling double gap.
Companies are hiring fewer freshers and calling it 'AI-first'.
The gig economy is absorbing displaced white-collar workers, not replacing them with better jobs.
malpractices: Unpaid 'AI internships' that are data labelling.
pro_claims: Routine cognitive work is being unbundled; the entry-level ladder is shrinking.
Indian IT's pyramid model relies on freshers; AI attacks the base.
The safety net is family and informal work, not unemployment insurance.
con_claims: India's demographic dividend and domestic demand create new roles faster than automation removes them.
AI adoption inside Indian enterprises is slower than the conference circuit suggests.
The bigger risk is wage stagnation, not mass unemployment.

label: Online learning / edtech
unit: % of households paying for online learning
motion: Online learning has permanently changed how tier-2/3 India learns.
ground_reality: The winner is not the fanciest app; it is the teacher who replies on WhatsApp.
Parents pay for hope, not features.
Shared devices and data costs shape usage more than pedagogy.
Regional-language explainers outperform English lectures in tier-3/4.
malpractices: Teachers paid per enrolment, not per outcome.
pro_claims: Online learning solves the teacher-quality problem for aspirational families.
Hybrid models with local mentors are working; pure-app models are not.
Regional-language content is the real growth market.
con_claims: Screen learning without accountability is mostly entertainment.
The category's trust deficit is structural after refund scandals.
Offline coaching still wins on discipline and peer pressure.

label: Health insurance for the missing middle
motion: The missing middle will buy health insurance once claim trust improves.
ground_reality: People buy after a hospital event, not before it.
The agent is trusted more than the app, and often mis-sells.
Claim rejection stories travel faster than settlement stories.
Ayushman Bharat covers a lot, but not the private hospital bill.
malpractices: Pre-existing disease non-disclosure encouraged by agents.
Room-rent caps and sub-limits buried in the policy.
Network hospitals refuse cashless at the last minute.
pro_claims: One hospitalization can erase a decade of savings; the product is under-owned.
Bima Sugam and embedded insurance can cut distribution cost.
Trust, not price, is the binding constraint.
con_claims: The product is sold, not bought; mis-selling poisons the well.
For many households, the premium competes with school fees.
Government schemes crowd out private cover at the bottom.

label: Digital credit in rural India
unit: % of rural adults using formal credit
motion: Digital credit is empowering rural India more than it is trapping it.
ground_reality: The loan officer is often the only formal financial touchpoint.
Recovery calls to family members are a common coercive tactic.
SHG discipline works where individual apps fail.
The '5-minute loan' ad is a data-harvesting funnel as much as a credit product.
malpractices: Unauthorised apps access contacts and photos.
Rollover loans disguised as new credit.
pro_claims: Formal credit replaces the moneylender at a lower price for many borrowers.
SHG-linked credit has a better repayment record than individual app loans.
Instant liquidity for health shocks is genuinely welfare-improving.
con_claims: APR opacity turns a ₹5,000 loan into a ₹9,000 obligation.
Contact-book harvesting is a surveillance business model.
The poorest borrowers are the most profitable and the least protected.

label: Premiumisation of daily FMCG
unit: % of category spend on premium packs
motion: Tier-2/3 India is ready to pay a premium for everyday FMCG.
ground_reality: The ₹5 sachet is a cash-flow product, not a poor person's product.
Premium is often a gift or festival purchase, not a daily habit.
Fake and 'same-to-same' products punish premium brands in smaller markets.
The kirana recommendation still outsells the Instagram ad.
malpractices: Counterfeit premium packs in tier-3 wholesale.
pro_claims: Aspiration is real, and premium packs are a low-cost way to signal it.
D2C and quick commerce have lowered trial costs.
Tier-2/3 is where the next 100 million premium buyers live.
con_claims: The sachet habit is rational; premium is a occasional treat.
Fake products destroy the price-value equation.
A 20% premium is a 20% cut in quantity for a household on a fixed budget.

label: Regional OTT subscriptions
motion: Regional-language OTT will beat English content in India.
ground_reality: Telecom bundles are the real acquisition channel.
Password sharing is a feature for price-sensitive households.
Regional content travels across state borders; dubbing is a growth lever.
ARPU is low, so ad-tier and bundles dominate.
pro_claims: Regional content is the only scalable answer to India's language diversity.
Bundling with telecom solves price and discovery simultaneously.
Co-viewing makes the household, not the individual, the unit.
con_claims: ARPU is too low to sustain prestige content.
Piracy and password sharing cap revenue.
Too many apps create subscription fatigue.

label: Rooftop solar for homes
price_note: ₹1.2-2.5 lakh for 3-5 kW; subsidy up to ₹78,000
motion: Rooftop solar will become the default middle-class home upgrade by 2030.
ground_reality: The installer, not the panel, determines the experience.
Apartment roofs and rented homes are excluded by default.
Net-metering delays can stretch to months.
The subsidy is real, but the paperwork is a filter.
pro_claims: A 3 kW system can cut a ₹3,000 monthly bill to near zero.
Subsidy and solar loans have shortened payback to 4-6 years.
Peer installation is the strongest predictor of adoption.
con_claims: Upfront cost excludes the households that need it most.
Installer quality is the real risk, not panel efficiency.
Renters and apartment dwellers are structurally excluded.

label: Gig work as a career
unit: % of young workers considering gig work
motion: Gig work is a stepping stone, not a trap, for young India.
ground_reality: The bike is a capital asset; the rider is the depreciating one.
Incentive structures change weekly and are not transparent.
Accident insurance is often a PDF, not a payout.
Women riders face safety and customer bias.
malpractices: Fuel and maintenance costs hidden in headline earnings.
pro_claims: Gig work absorbs surplus labour and provides immediate cash.
Flexibility is real for students and caregivers.
Platforms have lowered the cost of finding work.
con_claims: The flexibility is one-sided; the algorithm sets the terms.
Headline earnings hide vehicle, fuel and health costs.
No portability of benefits means every transition is a reset.

label: Women returning to work
motion: Indian families will normalise women's paid work within a generation.
ground_reality: The unpaid care economy is the hidden subsidy.
Safety is a transport and lighting issue, not only an attitude issue.
Remote work opened a door, but hybrid mandates are closing it.
Mothers are asked about 'commitment' in interviews; fathers are not.
malpractices: Safety committees that exist only on paper.
pro_claims: Female LFPR rose from 23.3% to 41.7% in six years; the direction is clear.
Remote and flexible work disproportionately benefits women.
Childcare and safe transport are the highest-leverage interventions.
con_claims: The rise is partly distress-driven, not opportunity-driven.
Safety and care burdens are structural, not attitudinal.
Without childcare, the gains reverse at the first child.

label: WhatsApp misinformation
motion: Fact-checking can meaningfully reduce misinformation in Indian family groups.
ground_reality: The forward is an act of care, not stupidity.
Correction from a family elder works; correction from a stranger backfires.
Local-language fact-checks spread slower than the original.
AI voice clones are the next trust shock.
malpractices: AI voice clones of relatives asking for money.
pro_claims: Prebunking and local-language corrections measurably reduce sharing.
Family-group interventions outperform platform labels.
Media literacy is a scalable public good.
con_claims: Corrections rarely reach the people who shared the original.
Identity-protective cognition beats facts.
Platform incentives reward outrage, not accuracy.

label: Agri drones and advisory
unit: % of farmers using paid advisory/drone services
motion: Agri drones will reach small farmers faster than tractors did.
ground_reality: A farmer with 1.5 acres cannot justify owning a drone; the service model is the only path.
The local input dealer is the incumbent trust node.
Advisory without input credit is a hobby.
Language and literacy shape the interface more than the algorithm.
malpractices: Advisory tied to a single chemical brand.
pro_claims: Service-based drone spraying solves the capital problem for smallholders.
FPO aggregation creates the trust and scale that individual apps lack.
Advisory plus input credit is the winning bundle.
con_claims: Small holdings make unit economics brutal.
Trust is with the dealer, not the app.
One bad spray season destroys adoption for years.

label: BNPL and young credit
motion: BNPL is a useful credit ladder for young Indians, not a debt trap.
ground_reality: The 0% EMI is funded by the merchant, not the fairy godmother.
Young users treat credit limits as income.
Late fees are the real revenue line.
Credit education arrives after the first default.
malpractices: Credit limit increases targeted at vulnerable users.
pro_claims: BNPL gives thin-file users a credit history they can use later.
0% EMI aligns with festival cash-flow realities.
Responsible limits can improve financial inclusion.
con_claims: The product is designed to make spending feel painless.
Late fees and recovery practices target the least sophisticated.
A credit ladder without guardrails is a debt chute.

label: Vernacular AI assistants
unit: % of internet users using voice/vernacular AI
motion: Voice-first vernacular AI will bring the next 500 million Indians online.
ground_reality: Voice is the interface for the next billion, but dialect accuracy is uneven.
Trust is built through a human intermediary, not a chatbot.
Privacy concerns are real but often overridden by convenience.
Scam risk rises with every new voice channel.
malpractices: Data harvesting under the guise of free advice.
pro_claims: Voice removes the literacy and English bottleneck.
The next 500 million users will not type in English.
Human-assisted AI (ASHA, CSCs) is the adoption path.
con_claims: Dialect accuracy is not ready for high-stakes advice.
Trust requires accountability, not just a friendly voice.
Data and device constraints still exclude the poorest.

label: Coaching culture and student mental health
motion: The Indian coaching system creates more anxiety than opportunity.
ground_reality: The topper ad is a lottery winner, not a median outcome.
Hostel food, sleep and safety are part of the product.
Parents buy status as much as learning.
Mental health support is an afterthought.
pro_claims: Coaching solves a real information and discipline gap.
Regional-language coaching is democratising access.
Hybrid models can reduce the relocation cost.
con_claims: The system selects for endurance, not curiosity.
Mental health costs are externalised onto families.
The topper mythology hides the median outcome.

label: Custom hypothesis
price_note: Set a price in the brief
motion: The proposed idea will find mainstream acceptance in India within three years.
ground_reality: India is not one market; it is at least four consumption realities.
Trust is built locally and lost publicly.
Cash flow beats net worth in most purchase decisions.
pro_claims: The category solves a real, felt problem.
The adoption curve is already moving in the right direction.
Trusted local distribution is the unlock.
con_claims: The addressable market is narrower than the headline suggests.
Price and trust are bigger barriers than awareness.
The first bad experience can define the category.
